claims.text: Roughly 1,100 proteins are known to sit inside human mitochondria, the energy centers of the cell, according to the Texas A&M AgriLife release.
claims.quote: about 1,100 proteins exist within mitochondria
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: For the screen itself the authors built a curated list of 1123 proteins.
claims.quote: generated a curated list of 1123 proteins
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The team screened 630,003 protein pairs and assembled a compendium of 2,895 interactions, some already known and some new.
claims.quote: By screening 630,003 protein pairs, we create a compendium of 2,895 previously known and newly observed interactions
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (abstract via Europe PMC)

claims.text: Of the 630,003 possible pairings, the screen flagged 2,895 as likely interactions.
claims.quote: Out of the 630,003 possible protein pairs, the team cataloged 2,895 likely interactions.
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: AlphaFold-Multimer is a neural network trained to predict the structures of protein complexes made of more than one protein chain.
claims.quote: AlphaFold-Multimer (AFM) is a neural network model trained to predict the structures of multimeric protein complexes
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: Google DeepMind created AlphaFold-Multimer, according to the Texas A&M AgriLife release.
claims.quote: Google DeepMind created and unveiled AFM
claims.note: Narrowed on 2026-11-08 after panel round 2: the release's 'unveiled AFM in 2022' is a third-party date the release is not authoritative on, and DeepMind's own record appears to date the tool to 2021, so the year is not carried.
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: The Texas A&M team turned a structure prediction tool into a classifier for protein interactions across the mitochondrial proteome.
claims.quote: we repurpose the protein structure prediction algorithm AlphaFold Multimer (AFM) as a classification model to predict protein-protein interactions
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (abstract via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The authors picked a mean ipTM score of 0.5 as the line between interacting and non-interacting pairs. On their test set that cutoff gives 67% recall at a false discovery rate of about 15%.
claims.quote: we decided to use 0.5 as a cutoff to separate interacting from non-interacting pairs, which gives 67% recall at a false discovery rate of about 15%
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: At the 0.5 mean ipTM cutoff, the screen predicts 2895 interactions involving 1004 proteins.
claims.quote: Based on our cutoff of 0.5 mean ipTM score, we predict 2895 interactions (0.46%) involving 1004 proteins
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The paper says the full set of predictions carries an apparent false discovery rate of 15%.
claims.quote: at an apparent FDR of 15%
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The authors say AFM can predict direct protein interactions in the mitochondrial proteome with 85% precision.
claims.quote: protein-protein interactions in the mitochondrial proteome with 85% precision
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: On a precision-recall benchmark, using the mean ipTM score as the classifier recovered ~40% of all true positives at 90% precision.
claims.quote: ~40% of all true positives at 90% precision
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: More than half of the likely interactions had never been reported before, the release says.
claims.quote: More than half of them had never been reported before.
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: Checked against existing interaction databases, 57% of the predicted interactions were missing from all of them, so the paper counts them as previously unreported.
claims.quote: the remaining 57% were not present in these databases and thus represent previously unreported interactions
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The predictions gave 85 previously uncharacterized proteins their first probable interaction partners.
claims.quote: gave 85 previously uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: The team ran the same AFM analysis on 11 diverse eukaryotes and found interactions among the human hits that are conserved through evolution.
claims.quote: Extending the AFM-based analysis to 11 diverse eukaryotes identifies evolutionarily conserved interactions among human hits
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (abstract via Europe PMC)

claims.text: Lab work guided by the predictions points to protein interactions that make up the coenzyme Q metabolon.
claims.quote: nominate protein interactions that form the coenzyme Q metabolon
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (abstract via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The same experiments map the pathway that delivers copper inside mitochondria to cytochrome c oxidase.
claims.quote: metabolon and define the mitochondrial copper delivery pathway to cytochrome c oxidase
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (abstract via Europe PMC)

claims.text: Roughly two years of lab experiments confirmed several of the predicted partnerships in yeast and human cells.
claims.quote: About two years of laboratory experiments followed, confirming several of the predicted partnerships in yeast and human cells
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: The team has posted its predictions online for free use under the name MitoMatch.
claims.quote: made its predictions available as a free online resource, MitoMatch
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: MitoMatch is made up of the 2895 predicted interactions.
claims.quote: These 2895 interactions constitute MitoMatch
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: Mutations in nearly 30% of mitochondrial proteins have been tied to human disease.
claims.quote: mutations in nearly 30% of mitochondrial proteins have been linked to human diseases
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: The release cautions that cures for diseases linked to mitochondria may still be a long way off.
claims.quote: Cures for mitochondria-linked diseases may still be far into the future
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: The paper states a limitation of the approach. It can't give the binding affinity of an interacting pair.
claims.quote: a limitation of this approach is that it cannot provide binding affinities of the interaction pair
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The authors note that many predicted interactions may happen inside a larger complex and may not exist as true two-protein pairs.
claims.quote: in the context of a larger complex and may not exist as true heterodimers
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The computing behind the work came from Texas A&M High Performance Research Computing.
claims.quote: advanced computing resources provided by the Texas A&M High Performance Research Computing
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The release names Texas A&M High Performance Research Computing and The Welch Foundation among the study's supporters.
claims.quote: Texas A&M High Performance Research Computing and The Welch Foundation
claims.document: AgriLife Today, Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria

claims.text: The Texas A&M authors are in the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics at Texas A&M University in College Station.
claims.quote: Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX, USA
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (abstract via Europe PMC)

claims.text: MitoMatch is online at mitomatch.web.app.
claims.quote: Our dataset, which we have named MitoMatch ( mitomatch.web.app ), consists of 2895
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

claims.text: The screen found at least one interacting partner for 85 uncharacterized proteins.
claims.quote: we identified at least one interacting partner for 85 uncharacterized proteins
claims.document: Nature Communications, The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome (full text via Europe PMC)

rejected.reason: Europe PMC gives electronicPublicationDate 2026-08-25 as a field, not a quotable sentence. The release of November 5th came after the paper.
Neither source gives a GPU hour figure. The paper names the FASTER cluster at TAMU-HPRC with no count.

rejected.finding: number of protein pairs tested experimentally
rejected.reason: The paper gives no count of pairs tested in the lab. The release says only several.

rejected.finding: a false negative rate or a third of true interactions missed
rejected.reason: No false negative rate is stated. A third missed would be computed from 67% recall, so it is rejected.

rejected.finding: 'this approach cannot define direct binary interactions' as an AFM limitation
rejected.reason: The sentence is about crosslinking mass spectrometry, not AFM.

rejected.finding: transient interactions as an AFM limitation
rejected.reason: The sentence describes the interactions, not a limitation of the screen.

rejected.finding: 85% of orphan mitochondrial proteins given a partner
rejected.reason: Contradicts the count of 85 uncharacterized proteins in the abstract, results and release. Only the count is claimed.
Set sizes were not checked as verbatim strings.

rejected.finding: the release's mention of 11 eukaryotes or the coenzyme Q metabolon
rejected.reason: The release mentions neither. c16 to c18 rest on the paper's abstract.

rejected.finding: who built AlphaFold-Multimer, sourced to the paper
rejected.reason: The paper names no builder. c6 rests on the release.
Answered 403. Paper claims use the ebi.ac.uk REST endpoints.

rejected.finding: Washington University School of Medicine role
rejected.reason: The release names the collaborator but not its part in the experiments.
